content.value_statement: Complex incidents often spread across logs, traces, services, and recent deployments. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured workflow for finding causes and planning fixes.
actual_capabilities: Classifies errors by severity, type, observability pattern, and user impact.
Guides root-cause analysis using reproduction steps, call-chain review, and recent-change checks.
Explains stack trace review, structured logging, correlation IDs, and distributed tracing workflows.
Provides retry, error boundary, validation, monitoring, alerting, and incident response patterns.
Helps produce incident summaries, timelines, root causes, fixes, tests, and prevention actions.
limitations: Requires relevant logs, stack traces, error reports, traces, or service context from the user.
Cannot access private telemetry, production systems, or vendor dashboards unless the user provides data.
Does not replace approval, rollback planning, or incident command for production changes.
Code samples are reference patterns and must be adapted before use in real systems.

use_cases.title: Investigate a Production Incident
use_cases.description: Build an evidence-based timeline, isolate affected services, and identify likely root causes.

use_cases.title: Debug a Recurring Application Error
use_cases.description: Group repeated failures, inspect stack traces, and propose fixes with validation steps.

use_cases.title: Improve Error Observability
use_cases.description: Design logging, tracing, alerting, and error handling improvements for future incidents.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize an Error
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner triage for a single error message or stack trace.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this error message and stack trace. Identify the error type, likely origin, missing context, and the first three checks I should run.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Root Cause
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate investigation with logs and recent changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these logs, timestamps, deployment notes, and stack traces. Build a timeline, list competing root-cause hypotheses, and rank them by evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Production Mitigation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced incident response for an active service issue.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this incident context to propose immediate mitigations, validation checks, rollback criteria, customer impact notes, and follow-up fixes. Flag any action that needs approval.

prompt_templates.title: Design Prevention Controls
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced reliability improvement after an incident.
prompt_templates.prompt: Given this post-incident analysis, design prevention work across tests, alerts, tracing, error handling, dashboards, and release safeguards. Prioritize by risk reduction.

output_examples.input: A payment service shows rising timeout errors after a deployment.
output_examples.output: The skill returns an incident timeline, affected components, likely database pool exhaustion, mitigation options, validation checks, and prevention tasks.

output_examples.input: A recurring stack trace appears only under high load.
output_examples.output: The skill separates symptoms from root causes, suggests reproduction experiments, identifies missing telemetry, and proposes targeted code and test changes.

output_examples.input: A team wants better visibility into distributed request failures.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends correlation IDs, trace propagation, structured logs, alert thresholds, dashboard checks, and data redaction practices.

best_practices: Provide exact timestamps, error messages, stack traces, deployment events, and affected services.
Redact secrets and personal data before sharing logs or diagnostic samples.
Validate each hypothesis with evidence before changing production systems.
anti_patterns: Do not paste sensitive tokens, customer data, or full private logs without redaction.
Do not apply production fixes without approval, rollback criteria, and monitoring.
Do not treat a symptom, such as a timeout, as the root cause without tracing upstream causes.

faq.question: What kinds of errors can this skill analyze?
faq.answer: It can analyze runtime errors, integration failures, performance issues, configuration problems, and production incidents.

faq.question: Does it need access to my production systems?
faq.answer: No. It works from the evidence you provide, such as logs, stack traces, traces, metrics, and incident notes.

faq.question: Can it write or deploy fixes automatically?
faq.answer: No. It can propose fixes, tests, and mitigations, but production changes still need normal approval and rollout controls.

faq.question: Can it help with observability design?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for structured logging, correlation IDs, tracing, dashboards, alerts, and error tracking.

faq.question: Is it suitable for post-incident reviews?
faq.answer: Yes. It can help organize timelines, root causes, contributing factors, corrective actions, and prevention work.

faq.question: How should I prepare data before using it?
faq.answer: Collect relevant evidence, remove secrets and personal data, and include service names, versions, timestamps, and recent changes.
